A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGMMD research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-H are readable and support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original helix and circle simulations, image-generation experiments, and quantitative MNIST denoising comparisons in Table 1.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds posterior-sampling, inpainting, intrinsic-dimension and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The ECMMD objective, nearest-neighbor construction and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new two-moons experiment introduces residual MLP and full-covariance Gaussian-mixture MDN generator variants with LayerNorm blocks (Appendix C.3.2), extending the model instantiations within the existing framework.

E1.justification: V2 adds two-moons posterior inference, FashionMNIST half-image inpainting, and synthetic conditional-regression scenarios addressing intrinsic dimensionality and kernel sensitivity. Circle evaluation also extends to low-density conditioning at X=4. MNIST, CelebA-HQ and STL10 were already evaluated in v1, including its appendices.

E2.justification: V2 adds two- and three-layer MAF conditional normalizing flows to circle comparisons, SNPE with MAF to the two-moons experiment, and distilled diffusion to the existing MNIST denoising comparison. These substantially extend the evaluated alternatives beyond v1's GCDS, WGAN and standard conditional diffusion.

E3.justification: Added studies introduce conditional-mean and conditional-standard-deviation MSE evaluation at fixed conditioning inputs, ambient dimensions from 25 to 500, and kernel, neighborhood and batch-size sweeps. The kernel study specifies 5,000 training samples. For the retained MNIST comparison, Table 1 removes FID and Inception Score while retaining PSNR, SSIM and timing.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained noise-level comparisons and training snapshots, v2 adds intrinsic-dimension sensitivity (Figure 9), low-density conditioning checks against flows (Figure 10), kernel-bandwidth and neighborhood-size ablations (Table 2), and batch-size effects with tail-region plots (Figure 18). These substantially expand robustness and practical sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: V2 specifies that Table 2 averages MSE over 100 repetitions; v1 provides no comparable experimental repetition counts. Figure 9 also introduces shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning. This is limited new statistical reporting, not evidence that retained experiments received additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds distilled diffusion with PSNR 10.658, SSIM 0.508 and 0.00092 seconds/image; the shared diffusion and CGMMD entries retain their reported PSNR, SSIM and timings. FID and Inception Score results are removed. New figures and Table 2 report dimensionality, sensitivity, inpainting and flow-comparison findings, including SNPE capturing two-moons crescents more accurately than CGMMD.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 becomes Theorem 4.4, restricting k_n from o(n^gamma), 0<gamma<1, to o(sqrt(n)) and replacing the displayed nearest-neighbor term n^(-(1-gamma)/d) with n^(-1/(2d)), up to logarithms. Equation (4.3) changes expected characteristic-function integral convergence to convergence in probability. V2 also defines intrinsic covering dimension and claims corresponding dimensional adaptation. Appendix E revises concentration bounds and corrects event indicators.

C1.justification: The central adversary-free optimization, one-shot sampling and convergence claims remain. V2's new conclusion explicitly includes inpainting in its empirical claims and qualifies benchmark ambitions generally as demonstrating flexibility and supporting theory; v1 made the qualification about not targeting state-of-the-art performance specifically for STL10 super-resolution.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of intrinsic-dimensional adaptation and kernel, neighborhood and batch-size tradeoffs. It acknowledges incomplete recovery of two-moons crescents, discusses distilled diffusion's competing PSNR/SSIM advantages, and clarifies that the experimental nearest-neighbor implementation is quadratic despite the near-linear computational possibility. These materially sharpen applicability and limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access URL, default batch size 200, Gaussian bandwidth sqrt(p), manual neighborhood selection, brute-force nearest-neighbor implementation details, and architecture/package information for new flow and posterior experiments. These are additional disclosures; they do not establish changes to retained implementations. ResNet-18/PCA preprocessing and image-generator descriptions were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Appendix A expands the closest-prior-work discussion to DISCO Nets and MMD gradient-flow samplers, including Arbel, Hagemann, Hertrich and Galashov and colleagues. It explicitly distinguishes CGMMD from a flow-based approach addressing the same conditional-sampling problem through formulation, kernel flexibility and theoretical guarantees. This substantively expands research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract, introduction, method exposition and appendix prose is retained. V2 adds a conclusion, acknowledgments and impact statement, moves the contents to the supplementary materials, shortens some headings and pseudocode, and updates author information. These are localized structural and editorial changes.

P2.justification: V2 retypesets the main text and references in two columns, resizes and rearranges existing figures, and moves the STL10 visualization into the main text. Table 1 gains a comparator row and loses two metric columns. New experimental plots, an inpainting montage and the four-panel sensitivity table substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited comparator coverage and lack of systematic sensitivity evidence. The distilled-diffusion and flow comparisons, explicit two-moons failure case, and kernel/batch-size analyses make strengths, weaknesses and practical choices much better supported. Added code-access and implementation disclosures further help reproducibility. Removed FID/Inception Score results and undefined Figure 9 bands reduce reporting completeness, but these costs do not outweigh the stronger, more balanced empirical assessment.
